reviews.verdict: No look-ahead and no fill bug found. An independent EA rebuild reproduces all 747 IS+VAL trades exactly, and the causality and timing probes pass. But the PASS only holds for a fully automated 24/5 EA, and PF is sensitive to fill quality. Alerts-first or semi-manual execution brings VAL PF to 0.87-1.24, or IS t below 2.

issues.description: No look-ahead in the code the finalist uses (strategy._donchian_stop, _first_touch, add_trading_days, exit_index, gl.bars, gl.atr, gl.entry_index, sim._run). The OCO side is picked by a forward scan in _first_touch. That scan is equivalent to a real-time OCO: no order exists before the first touch, and nothing after the fill bar changes the order. Channel and ATR use only complete 4h bars. M1 bars are labelled by their start time, the data is in UTC, and DST is handled correctly.
issues.evidence: refimpl.py is a sequential bar-by-bar EA written from the text rule (my own 4h bins, Wilder ATR, zoneinfo time exit, swap). It matches the engine on 499/499 IS and 248/248 VAL trades: same side, entry/exit price (max diff 4.6e-13), exit time and R. The NY-17h vs bin-boundary decision clock gives identical results. I hand-checked 14 random IS trades from raw M1 rows by pandas slicing (channel, ATR, first touch, fill, trailing path, exit, swap nights, R): 14/14 match within 1e-13. Truncation probes: levels and ATR identical at 120/120 random decisions on data cut at the decision. With data cut just before the fill bar, no order exists (40/40). With data cut 2 bars after the fill and the post-fill bar garbled (+/-5%), the order is unchanged (40/40). Ticks (Jul 2025) match M1 bar [T,T+1m) 100% vs 6-9% for [T-1m,T). Widest spread falls at 20:58 UTC in summer and 21:59 UTC in winter, i.e. 17:00 NY in both. 0 NaT time exits. 0 OCO ties over all 2646 resolved windows.
issues.effect_on_results: None. Deliberate early activation by 1-2 M1 bars (a look-ahead) leaves PF unchanged (IS 1.350 / VAL 1.294). Early by 5 bars: 1.342 / 1.287. Minute-level timing does not drive the result.

issues.description: The simulated execution needs a fully automated EA running 24/5. It places an OCO at every 4h close, including 00:00 and 04:00 UTC (01:00-06:00 Paris). It must cancel the other leg itself, because MT5 has no native OCO. It recomputes the trailing stop at every M1 close. The trader's alerts-first or manual plan cannot reproduce this. The variants a French retail trader would realistically run lose much of the VAL edge, or fail the IS t>=2 criterion.
issues.evidence: refimpl2 variants, IS / VAL PF. Skip the 00 and 04 UTC decisions: 1.335 / 1.13 (VAL t 0.70). Leave the evening OCO unchanged until the next 08:00 UTC: 1.368 / 1.236 (t 1.22). Same plus MT4/MT5 terminal-style trailing, which only starts once profit exceeds 2xATR (approximated at M1 granularity): 1.228 (IS t 1.68, fails) / 1.317. Trail moved only at each 4h alert: 1.267 (IS t 1.90, fails) / 1.282. Only 16/20 UTC decisions: 1.32 / 0.868. Orders placed late: +60 min 1.343 / 1.228; +120 min 1.177 / 1.104. Fills in the 00-08 UTC windows supply 18.8 of 61.5 R on IS (31%) and 15.0 of 24.7 R on VAL (61%).
issues.effect_on_results: The PASS figures (1.35 / 1.29) are valid only for the automated rule. Realistic manual or alerts variants: VAL PF 0.87-1.24, or IS PF about 1.23-1.27 with t below 2.

issues.description: Fills at the exact level in fast markets are optimistic, and PF is steeply sensitive to that. Stop entries fill at max(level, open) and trailing exits at min(stop, open), plus 1.5 bp per side. Real breakouts and stop-outs often happen in large M1 bars, e.g. 2013-06-26 01:05: $9.5 range through the sell level; 2014-09-05 12:30 NFP: $10 through the trailing stop.
issues.evidence: Ticks (n=25, Jun-Dec 2025): tick fills are worse than M1-at-level by $0.161 on entry and $0.413 on exit, i.e. $0.574 = 0.0135 R per round trip. The engine slippage budget is $1.12 = 0.0287 R; 3/25 trades exceed it. This implies traders pay 9% (entry) and 21% (exit) of the trigger bar's range beyond the level. Stress (extra fraction of that range on top of the 1.5 bp), IS / VAL PF: 10% 1.292 / 1.254; 25% 1.21 / 1.187; 50% 1.087 / 1.083. Tick-calibrated 9%/21% replacing the slippage: 1.388 / 1.35. Same on top of the slippage (double count): 1.271 / 1.236.
issues.effect_on_results: On the tick evidence the base model is adequate to slightly conservative. Sensitivity is about -0.06 PF per extra 10% of trigger-bar overshoot. The calibration rests on 25 trades from one half-year.

issues.description: Trailing granularity is ambiguous inside spike bars. An M1 bar cannot tell whether its high or low came first. The engine applies the trail only after the bar closes; tick-based trailing (OnTick EA) would exit differently in flash-spike minutes.
issues.evidence: Bound where the favourable extreme comes first in every bar: IS 1.319 / VAL 1.204. An open/high/low/close path heuristic gives results identical to base. 11 IS trades are affected, all in flash minutes (2013-07-21 22:12, 2015-07-20 01:29, 2017-06-26 08:01, 2021-08-08 22:51, ...), e.g. 2021-08-06 short R +8.33 vs +4.36, 2015-07-15 short +5.29 vs +8.58.
issues.effect_on_results: An EA trailing tick-by-tick would land between base and IS -0.03 / VAL -0.09 PF. An EA trailing exactly at M1 closes matches the sim.

issues.description: Results depend on implementation details that an MT5 EA can easily get wrong: the UTC 4h grid (MT5 brokers use NY-close server time, UTC+2/+3), and a channel that includes the just-closed bar.
issues.evidence: Grid offset +1h / +2h / +3h: IS 1.304 / 1.284 / 1.349 (t 2.11 / 1.94 / 2.32), VAL 1.354 / 1.264 / 1.256; the track found 1.313 IS on the broker server grid. Channel excluding the just-closed bar: IS 1.285 (t 2.03) / VAL 1.271. Levels one 4h bar stale: IS 1.272 (t 1.94) / VAL 1.234. Level source is robust: bid / ask / true per-minute mid gives IS 1.382 / 1.349 / 1.351, VAL 1.288 / 1.331 / 1.297.
issues.effect_on_results: A typical off-by-one or broker-grid EA would lose about 0.04-0.08 IS PF and could fail t>=2. VAL stays at 1.23-1.35. Smooth degradation, no collapse.

issues.description: The VAL result moved noticeably with data-hole patching, so it depends on data completeness. The patch files themselves are correctly aligned.
issues.evidence: The patch added 77,215 M1 bars, 39,637 of them in 2022-2025. Audit unpatched vs patched: VAL n 243 to 248, PF 1.232 to 1.294, R 19.3 to 24.7. IS PF 1.356 to 1.35. 30/30 sampled patch files align at shift 0 with 100% close match on overlapping minutes (shifts -180..+180 min tested).
issues.effect_on_results: VAL PF +0.06 from patching alone. The 2026 holdout needs the same patching (holdout.py skips Dec 24-Jan 2).

issues.description: End-of-data truncation: exit_index maps a time exit beyond the data to the last bar, and the trade is labelled 'time'.
issues.evidence: The last VAL trade (short, entered 2025-12-31 05:53 UTC) is force-closed at 21:58 UTC the same day as 'time' (R -0.36, 8997 min before its scheduled exit). In holdout.py this position will carry into 2026 and block new entries until it exits.
issues.effect_on_results: Negligible on VAL PF (one trade, -0.36 R).

issues.description: Pitfalls for live and alert tooling (not backtest leaks). On truncated or live data, make_orders drops the newest decision until at least one bar after the fill exists, because keep &= xi > hit_i and xi is clipped to the last bar. It also sets exit_i to the last bar for open trades. exit_index moves exits before closures using future knowledge of where the data exists. bars_cached is keyed on id(m1), len and endpoints, so a frame modified in place could get stale bars.
issues.evidence: Truncation probe (b) with data cut right after the fill: 0/40 orders emitted. Cutting 2 bars later: 40/40 identical. 309/20800 scheduled exits are moved earlier: holidays, plus 27 at end of data. Among taken trades, all 8 IS and 3 VAL time exits are at the schedule; the only moved one is the end-of-data trade. Max hold 167.8 h, never later than scheduled.
issues.effect_on_results: None on the reported numbers. The alert generator must not reuse make_orders unchanged.

issues.description: Other fidelity checks passed.
issues.evidence: Cost stress x1.5 with the OCO side re-resolved under the stressed spreads: IS 1.255 / VAL 1.200 (engine 1.256 / 1.215). Fills blocked at rollover and Sunday open: IS 1.338-1.35 / VAL 1.283-1.286. Entries in news minutes: 45 IS (+4.9 R) and 20 VAL (+4.9 R); PF without them 1.356 / 1.253. Data holes inside trades: 25 IS trades, all US-holiday early closes or Christmas/New Year closures, plus 4 short outages (21-120 min) with price moves of $2.1 or less. Gap fills: 10 IS / 6 VAL. Stops hit on the fill bar: 1 / 1. Swap triple on Friday instead of Wednesday: PF +/-0.002. Lot-step rounding at 1% risk ($2k-$100k accounts): PF in $ IS 1.32-1.35, VAL 1.29-1.42. Micro-perturbations, 20 seeds each (level noise +/-$0.05 and +/-$0.50, random 0-2 min delay, trail +/-1%): IS PF 1.331-1.419, VAL 1.278-1.338. The one-position trade path is stable, so the taken vs every-signal gap is not a micro-path accident.
issues.effect_on_results: None material.

recommendations: Treat the PASS as conditional on an automated EA that replicates the rule exactly. Build UTC-grid H4 bars from M1, not the broker's server-time H4 bars. Use a 60-bar mid channel that includes the just-closed bar. Implement OCO with cancel-on-fill (MT5 has none natively). Recompute the trailing SL at each M1 close from bid-high / ask-low (not OnTick, not the terminal's built-in trailing). Time exit at the decision's NY clock + 5 trading days - 5 min.

For the alerts-first phase, pre-register the manual variant that will actually be followed and report its backtest. With the evening OCO left until 08 UTC and M1 trailing via an EA: IS 1.368 / VAL 1.236. With the terminal trailing it fails IS t>=2. Do not expect the PASS figures from manual execution.
Report the 2026 holdout under the primary model and also under one execution stress: +10% trigger-bar overshoot, and the tick-like trailing bound.
Handle the open-position state at 2025-12-31 explicitly in holdout.py. The last 2025 trade is currently closed as 'time' at end of data; it should carry into 2026.

In live phase 2, log trigger level vs actual fill on every entry and stop-out. If the mean round-trip shortfall exceeds about 0.03 R (the modelled slippage), expect about -0.06 PF per extra 10% of trigger-bar overshoot.

Do not reuse make_orders unchanged as the live alert generator. It omits the newest decision until a bar after the fill exists, and sets exit_i to the last bar for open trades. Avoid the id()-keyed bar cache when frames can be modified in place.
Apply the same hole-patching to the 2026 data (holdout.py excludes Dec 24 to Jan 2): data completeness alone moved VAL PF by +0.06.

reviews.lens: STATISTICAL SKEPTIC (selection, empirical nulls, bootstrap, concentration, stability, holdout power)
reviews.candidate: trend/donch4h_stop (Turtle-style 60x4h channel breakout, OCO stops, 2xATR14(4h) initial and trailing stop, 5-NY-day time stop, one position at a time)
reviews.verdict: The edge is not demonstrated. Breakout persistence in 2013-21 looks real, but the IS t does not survive the search (RC p 0.15), a drift-only world passes the VAL test 48% of the time, and VAL every-signal is about 0. My estimate: P(positive after-cost edge going forward) ≈ 0.3 (range 0.15-0.45), P(as large as measured) ≈ 0.1. ~10 months of holdout cannot settle it.

issues.description: IS significance does not survive the search. The candidate was the best of 48 correlated trend configs logged before the decision, and the only PASS among 6 tracks and 301 logged trials. Tested against a zero-net-edge null, its t=2.35 is ordinary for the best of a search this size.
issues.evidence: Correlation of weekly R across the 48 configs gives N_eff 21 (Li-Ji) / 22 (Galwey) / 37 (Nyholt). White Reality Check p=0.151, Hansen SPA_c p=0.138. Multivariate-normal max-t: P(max t>=2.35)=0.17. Single-test p=0.009. Boundary null (candidate R recentred to 0, week clusters): alpha_IS=1.5%, alpha_VAL=27.8%. P(>=1 trial passes IS+VAL by luck) for N_eff=21/50/130/300: boundary 8/19/42/71%; exact rule on day-mirrored gold 6.5/15/34/62%; same with yearly drift kept 1.5/3.4/8.7/19%; random-entry nulls <=4% even at 300. Project N_eff is about 80-140 (181 trials have IS t>-1; trend-track N_eff/M ratio 0.44-0.77).
issues.effect_on_results: Against realistic nulls, a search of this size produces one 'PASS' by chance with roughly 15-40% probability. The PASS label alone is weak evidence.

issues.description: The VAL criterion (PF>=1.10, expectancy>0) has little power against gold's 2022-25 rally. Strategies with no timing skill but the same long tilt pass it often, and the candidate's VAL PF is not extreme under those nulls.
issues.evidence: Exact rule on day-mirrored gold with the calendar-year drift kept (100 histories): VAL pass 48%, P(VAL PF>=1.294)=11%. Random long-only entries with the identical exits: VAL pass 76%, P(PF>=1.294)=28%. Random entries 63% long: 24% / 4.2%. Random side: 12% / 1.6%. Signal times with random side: 3.1% / 0%. Candidate VAL t=1.49 (month-cluster t 1.48). Week-cluster bootstrap P(exp<=0)=6.3%, PF 90% CI [0.98, 1.68].
issues.effect_on_results: Passing VAL is worth a likelihood ratio of only about 1-2 for edge versus no edge. It is mostly what gold's 2022-25 drift would produce for a long-tilted trend rule.

issues.description: At the signal level the breakout has no edge in VAL. The chain passes only because, in VAL, the first breakout after being flat beat the continuation breakouts that the one-position rule skips. That pattern was absent in IS (taken ≈ skipped).
issues.evidence: Every-signal mean R ± month-clustered SE: IS +0.126 ± 0.079, VAL -0.009 ± 0.068 (z=-1.95 vs the IS chain mean). VAL skipped trades -0.047 ± 0.076 (z=-2.24). Taken minus skipped: IS -0.003 (bootstrap sd 0.073), VAL +0.147 (sd 0.061). That gap sits at the 98th percentile of the day-mirror null. Real VAL every-signal PF 0.977 is below the drift-kept null median of 1.083. Joint GLS estimate of a common VAL edge (taken and skipped, corr 0.64): +0.051 ± 0.064 R, z=0.79; likelihood ratio for edge-as-measured vs none = 0.83. Random alert dropout pulls VAL PF toward 0.98: median 1.26 at q=0.10, 1.19 at q=0.33, 1.13 at q=0.50, while IS stays 1.29-1.33. The pattern repeats on every 4h grid alignment (VAL every-signal 0.96-1.04, chain 1.26-1.35).
issues.effect_on_results: If, as IS indicates, which signals the chain takes is unrelated to their outcome, VAL is close to neutral evidence. The VAL pass depends on a VAL-specific chain effect that is not expected to carry forward.

issues.description: The result rests on a handful of fat-tailed trades, weeks and one year in each period.
issues.evidence: Skew 2.1 (IS) / 1.7 (VAL). Top 5% of trades = 145% (IS) / 150% (VAL) of net R. Removing the top 15 IS trades (3.0%) or top 7 VAL trades (2.8%) wipes out net R. PF without the top 10 trades: IS 1.079, VAL 0.905. Weeks needed to wipe out net R: 14 of 346 (IS), 6 of 164 (VAL). 2025 = 64% of VAL R; VAL without 2025: PF 1.135, t 0.63; without 2025 and 2023: PF 1.015, t 0.06. IS without 2020: t 1.83; without 2016: t 1.91 (both below 2); without the best two years: t 1.34.
issues.effect_on_results: Small changes in which trades occur flip the conclusion, for example a missed alert or a different 2025. PF in a short window is extremely noisy.

issues.description: The edge has been long-side, regime-dependent beta since 2017, and the in-sample edge weakened over time.
issues.evidence: IS halves: 2013-16 PF 1.47 (t 2.03, shorts PF 1.55); 2017-21 PF 1.26 (t 1.32, shorts PF 0.79). Shorts 2017-2025: -21.2 R over 222 trades. VAL long PF 1.69 (t 2.40) vs short 0.72 (t -1.20), Welch p=0.011. VAL profit comes entirely from longs while gold is above its 60-day MA (+35.0 R, t 2.56); every other regime/side cell is -10.3 R. Every-signal VAL longs PF 1.10 vs random-timed longs 1.20; shorts 0.50 vs 0.63. In IS, all profit came from the lowest ATR tercile (+63.5 R, t 3.11); in VAL the terciles are even, so that subgroup is unstable.
issues.effect_on_results: 2026 results will be driven mainly by gold's direction. A long-only profit in a rising 2026 cannot be told apart from beta.

issues.description: The edge is thin compared with execution latency. The IS pass needs resting OCO stop orders at every 4h close. Entering after an alert, even one minute late, fails the pre-registered IS criteria.
issues.evidence: True side, market entry d minutes after the first touch. IS: d=1 PF 1.25, t 1.78 (fails t>=2); d=5 1.238/1.70; d=15 1.175/1.28 (also fails PF>=1.2); d=60 1.106/0.82. VAL: 1.246 / 1.186 / 1.124 / 1.192. Each minute of latency at the breakout costs about 0.03 R of a 0.12 R edge.
issues.effect_on_results: For an 'alerts first, I decide' workflow, realistic latency removes 25-50% of the measured edge. Manual coverage of the 00/04 UTC decisions is impractical.

issues.description: A ~10-month holdout (~50 trades) cannot discriminate edge from no edge. The protocol's PF>1 criterion is close to a coin flip under both hypotheses.
issues.evidence: 2-week block resampling, ~50 trades. H1 (edge as measured, +0.115 R): PF median 1.30, 90% interval [0.55, 2.79], P(PF>1)=0.70. Half the measured edge: 1.12 [0.47, 2.41], 0.59. H0 (zero edge): 0.97 [0.39, 2.11], 0.47. H0 with random-entry cost drag: 0.87 [0.35, 1.89], 0.39. Empirical 10-month windows of random-entry nulls: median 0.84-0.87, P>1 0.33-0.34. Likelihood ratios H1 vs H0 by PF bin (<0.6 / 0.6-0.8 / 0.8-1.0 / 1.0-1.2 / 1.2-1.5 / >=1.5): 0.29-0.37 / 0.51-0.57 / 0.75-0.77 / 0.95-1.02 / 1.23-1.40 / 2.1-3.0. Protocol pass: 1.5-1.8; fail: 0.5-0.6. Confirming +0.115 R at 80% power needs ~590 trades (~10 years); +0.058 R needs ~2300 trades.
issues.effect_on_results: Starting from 0.30: a pass gives about 0.39-0.43, a fail about 0.17-0.20, PF>=1.5 about 0.48-0.57, PF<0.6 about 0.11-0.14. No 10-month outcome is decisive; a clear loss is the most informative.

issues.description: The audit's deflated Sharpe ratio (0.07) is mis-specified. It counts all 50 logged trials, including post-decision checks and the overlapping every-signal t of 4.32, and uses a cross-trial SR variance inflated by cost-negative 1h/VBO configs.
issues.evidence: Recomputed DSR: 0.09 with the empirical variance of all 48 and N=48 (similar to the audit); 0.46-0.63 with the variance of plausible configs and N=48/20; 0.54-0.90 with the null variance 1/n and N=48 to 5. With N_eff ≈ 20: about 0.63-0.69.
issues.effect_on_results: The DSR is inconclusive in both directions. Reality Check / SPA (p ≈ 0.14-0.15) is the better selection-adjusted measure.

issues.description: This is not luck relative to random timing. In 2013-21 the breakout timing carried real information, and the exit structure alone loses.
issues.evidence: Candidate IS PF 1.35 exceeds all 1000 random time+side runs (median 0.865, max 1.202; t mean -1.21, sd 0.95), all 1000 signal-time random-side runs (max 1.202), and all 200 synthetic day-mirrored histories (max 1.31; 2/100 passed IS, both failed VAL). IS every-signal PF 1.344 exceeds all 200 synthetic histories (max 1.27). At the signal times with the same entry mechanism: follow 1.25, fade 0.66, random 0.90; true side beats a quarter-tilt-preserving side permutation at p=0.03 in IS but only p=0.18 in VAL. No serial correlation (lag-1 -0.01, Ljung-Box p 0.75); cluster-robust t 2.32-2.34.
issues.effect_on_results: The question is not whether gold breakouts persisted in 2013-21 (they did) but whether that survives costs, selection and regime change. VAL says not at the signal level.

issues.description: Conclusion on probability: P(the traded chain has positive expectancy after the modelled costs going forward) ≈ 0.30, plausible range 0.15-0.45. P(edge >= the measured ~0.1 R/trade) ≈ 0.10. If real, the expected size is about +0.03 to +0.06 R/trade (PF ≈ 1.08-1.15), which execution latency or extra slippage can erase.
issues.evidence: Prior 0.10-0.15 for a short-horizon single-market breakout after retail costs (IS variance ratios ≈ 1; time-series momentum is documented mainly at 1-12 months). IS Bayes factor ≈ 2-5 (selection-adjusted p 0.14-0.17 vs zero net edge; far stronger vs random-entry nulls). VAL Bayes factor ≈ 0.8-1.4 (taken and skipped jointly) and at most 2-3 for the chain alone, discounted for long tilt. Cross-market ≈ 1: same parameters give IS PF 0.98-1.34 (mean ~1.12) and VAL 0.60-1.47 (mean ~0.97). Posterior odds ≈ 0.11-0.18 × 3 × 1.2 ≈ 0.4-0.65.
issues.effect_on_results: Treat the candidate as an unproven, low-conviction hypothesis, not a validated rule.

recommendations: Keep the PASS label as a protocol fact, but report it as low conviction: P(real) ≈ 0.3, expected true edge ≈ +0.03 to +0.06 R/trade (PF ≈ 1.1), not the measured +0.12 R. No real-money trading on the current evidence.

Before downloading 2026, write down how the holdout will be read. Compare it with same-period nulls run on 2026 data with this engine: signal times with random side, random long-only and short-only entries, and the drift-kept synthetic. Also report the every-signal PF and the long/short split. Bands: PF>=1.5 = weak support (LR 2-3); 0.8-1.5 = inconclusive; <0.7 = meaningful evidence against. A profit made only on longs while gold rises in 2026 does not count as evidence.

Replace the one-look holdout decision with sequential forward monitoring on paper/demo using resting OCO stops. Update a Bayesian posterior or run an SPRT on per-trade R (H1 +0.06 R, H0 0, sd 1.12 R) with a kill rule fixed in advance (for example cumulative R <= -10 R or posterior < 0.15). If ever implemented, use only pending OCO stop orders placed at every 4h close (EA or MT5 pending orders). An alert followed by a manual market order (>=1 min latency) loses 25-50% of the edge and fails the IS criteria, and the 00:00 and 04:00 UTC decisions cannot be covered by hand.

Do not adopt fixes suggested by these diagnostics (long-only, low-ATR filter, first-breakout-only logic, dropping shorts, a different grid). Each would be a new selection that has seen VAL. Register them as separate hypotheses for forward data only.

If it is ever traded: fixed-fractional risk <= 0.25-0.5% per trade, and never skip signals at discretion, since net R comes from about 3% of trades. Expect 8-11 R drawdowns and about 2/3 of weeks not positive.
Fix the audit's DSR (use N_eff ≈ 20, the null SR variance, and exclude post-decision and overlapping trials), and report Reality Check / SPA p ≈ 0.14-0.15 as the selection-adjusted IS significance.

reviews.lens: LIVE-EXECUTION REALISM for an MT5 retail account (EU/ESMA, French client)
reviews.verdict: The PASS does not carry over to the trader's planned 'alerts first, he decides' mode. Even a 1-minute-late market entry cuts IS PF from 1.35 to 1.24-1.26 (t<2), human hours lose the night trades (15% of IS trades but 24% of IS R; 65% of VAL R), and MT5's own trailing stop changes the exit rule (IS 1.21). Only broker-side OCO stops plus per-minute EA trailing on a 24/5 VPS reproduce the backtest, and plausible retail frictions still bring that down to IS 1.20 / VAL 1.16. The edge is small and fragile, and 0.5% risk needs about EUR 6-9k because of the 0.01-lot minimum.

issues.description: Entering at market after the alert is a different and weaker strategy. Any delay of 1 minute or more fails the pre-registered IS t>=2, so the planned execution mode ('alert, then he decides and enters') is not the strategy that passed.
issues.evidence: p1_delay.out, base IS PF 1.350 (t 2.35) / VAL 1.294. Model A1 (market entry N min after the theoretical stop fill, stop and trail re-anchored at 2 ATR, same time stop), IS / VAL PF: N=1 1.244 (t 1.73) / 1.255; N=5 1.239 (t 1.70) / 1.166; N=15 1.220 (t 1.56) / 1.104; N=60 1.137 (t 1.03) / 1.186; N=240 1.117 (t 0.89) / 1.095. Model B (EA mode 1 puts the fictive stop on the manual position, so exits match and only the entry is late; R in planned-risk units), IS / VAL: N=1 1.256 / 1.259; N=5 1.238 / 1.196; N=15 1.198 / 1.108; N=60 1.137 / 1.123; N=240 1.044 / 0.935. Model C (alerts only when the REAL position is flat, sequential) gives similar values: N=1 1.249 / 1.255, N=15 1.207 / 1.102. Mean IS chase cost, i.e. how much worse the late entry is, in R: +0.031 (N=1), +0.038 (N=5), +0.054 (N=15). It is skewed: median +0.009 R, p90 +0.17 R. The fastest breakouts, which are the winners, are the ones that run away. The engine's stop fill is realistic for a stop order sitting at the broker (the audit's tick check stays within the slippage budget), so the loss comes from the human delay, not from optimistic backtesting.
issues.effect_on_results: About 25% of the expectancy (0.123 to 0.090 R) is lost at N=1, about 30-35% at N=5-15, and more than 50% at N >= 60. IS criterion 2 (t>=2) fails for every N>=1. VAL PF is 1.10-1.20 for N = 5-15 and below 1 for N=240 under model B.

issues.description: Human availability. Breakouts that trigger at night (Paris time) are disproportionately profitable, so a trader who only acts while awake keeps the weaker part of the signal stream.
issues.evidence: p2_availability.out, instant execution of the subset whose trigger falls in the window: W1 (07-23 Paris, every day) IS PF 1.313 (t 1.94, n 423) / VAL 1.117 (n 197); W2 (Mon-Fri 08-20 Paris) IS 1.276 (t 1.63, n 376) / VAL 1.280 (n 167). Same subsets with a 5-min market entry: W1 1.203 / 1.028; W2 1.146 / 1.173. The 76 IS trades outside W1 (15% of trades) make +14.7 R (0.19 R/trade, against 0.11 inside W1). In VAL, the 51 trades outside W1 make +16.0 of the 24.7 R. Alerts cluster at 14-16h Paris (40%, US data releases); about 8 alerts per year fall at night. Entering night signals at 07:00 instead (if the theoretical trade is still open): IS 1.237 / VAL 1.166. Flat-gated (night triggers ignored, sequential) with a 5-min entry: W1 1.236 / 1.091; W2 1.159 / 1.116.
issues.effect_on_results: IS t falls below 2 even with instant fills. VAL PF drops to about 1.12 (W1) with instant fills and to 1.03-1.17 with a realistic 5-minute reaction.

issues.description: The every-minute 2-ATR trailing stop is part of the edge, and MT5 gives a retail trader no faithful way to run it without an EA on an always-on terminal. MT5's built-in trailing works differently: it is client-side, runs only while the desktop terminal is open, the mobile app does not have it, and it starts moving the SL only once open profit reaches the trailing distance.
issues.evidence: p2_availability.out. Built-in-style trailing (SL stays at the initial stop until profit >= 2 ATR, then trails) with entries from pending stops: IS PF 1.205 (t 1.54, n 445) / VAL 1.350; with 5-min manual entries: 1.158 / 1.201. Phone-only mode (5-min market entry while awake, SL moved by hand only at the in-window 4h closes, time exit brought forward into the window): W1 IS 1.178 (t 1.24) / VAL 1.050; W2 1.145 / 1.078. The lookahead lens's 'trail updated at 4h closes only' (p8_hours_manualtrail.out) gives IS 1.267 / VAL 1.282. The MT4 official help states the activation rule ('as soon as profit in points becomes equal to or higher than the specified level') and that the trailing stop does not work if the terminal is off; an MT5 forum post and broker manuals describe the same behaviour and its absence from the mobile app.
issues.effect_on_results: Exit realism alone moves IS PF from 1.35 to 1.18-1.27 and IS t below 2, unless an EA on a VPS pushes the server-side SL at every M1 close (median 18, p90 67 SL modifications per trade).

issues.description: The edge is thin compared with plausible retail execution costs. Each extra basis point of slippage per side costs about 0.023 R per trade, out of an expectancy of about 0.10-0.12 R.
issues.evidence: p7_costs_news.out, IS / VAL PF: slippage 3 bp per side on every market or stop fill 1.232 (t 1.66) / 1.186; 5 bp 1.102 / 1.061. Broker-like swaps of 8%/3% per year (long/short) 1.313 (t 2.15) / 1.259; 10%/4% 1.287 (t 1.99) / 1.235. p8_combos.out, retail combination (3 bp plus 8%/3% swaps): EA auto 1.199 (t 1.45) / 1.155; pending-orders-while-awake with EA trailing 1.206 / 1.121; same with hand-moved SL 1.166 / 1.060; phone-only mode 1.050 / 0.930. Fills in the first 5 minutes after 08:30, 10:00 or 14:00 ET are 43 of 499 IS trades; even +20 bp extra entry slippage on them only reaches IS 1.280 / VAL 1.232.
issues.effect_on_results: Under plausible retail frictions the best implementation sits at IS PF about 1.20 (t 1.45) and VAL about 1.16. That still meets the PF thresholds but fails the IS t threshold, and it leaves no margin for the human-execution losses above.

issues.description: Sensitivity to the broker's spread spike at the daily close (17:00 New York). The requested 'spreads x2 around the rollover' is harmless, but a retail-style spike in the 10 minutes before the 17:00 NY break stops out open trailing positions.
issues.evidence: p4_rollover.out, IS / VAL PF: x2 on 16:30-17:00 and 18:00-18:30 NY 1.360 / 1.302; x2 on 16:00-17:00 and 18:00-19:00 NY 1.359 / 1.302; x3 over the 2 hours 1.300 (t 2.09) / 1.301; x5 on 16:50-17:00 and 18:00-18:20 NY plus x2 on the rest of the 2 hours 1.065 (t 0.52) / 1.291. p4b_spike_decomp.out: x5 before the close only 1.089 / 1.306 (with entries unchanged, exits only: 1.158 / 1.290; 41 IS trades stopped by the spike, mean -0.79 R each); x5 at the reopen only 1.322 / 1.282. The Dukascopy data already have no bars from 17:00 to 17:59 NY, and the average close spread at 16:59 NY is about $1.0 (2013-21) and $1.4 (2025). The exit-only path reproduces the engine exactly (p4c_exitonly_parity.out).
issues.effect_on_results: Depends on the broker and is not visible in Dukascopy data. A large pre-close spike can remove about half of the IS edge. VAL is unaffected because 2022-25 stops are wider relative to the spread.

issues.description: Minimum lot size and economics. With 1 lot = 100 oz, the smallest trade (0.01 lot = 1 oz) already risks a full 2-ATR stop. Below a certain account size the trader cannot risk 0.5%, so actual risk per trade drifts and the R-based statistics stop describing the money outcome. On the smallest viable accounts, the expected profit is about the cost of the VPS that is needed to run the trailing stop.
issues.evidence: p5_sizing.out. Stop distance (2 x ATR14 on 4h bars) per oz: 2025 median $34.9 (p10 23.4, p90 65.7); Q4-2025 median $55.0 (p90 93.4); IS median $11.6. Account needed for 0.01 lot to equal the target risk: 0.5% needs $7.0k (EUR 6.0k) at the 2025 median and $11.0k (EUR 9.4k) at the Q4 median; 1% needs $3.5k (EUR 3.0k) and $5.5k. Keeping rounding error at 10% or less needs 10 times that. ESMA 1:20 margin is $168 per 0.01 lot at $3,358 and $211 at $4,227, i.e. 2.4% of equity at 0.5% risk and 4.8% at 1%, so leverage is not the constraint. A $2k account at a 0.5% target is forced to the minimum lot on 98% of VAL trades, with effective risk median 1.0%, p90 2.1%, max 5.1%. PF in dollars with minimum-lot sizing: IS $2k at 0.5% gives 1.20 against 1.35 in R; VAL gives 1.40 against 1.29. Expected return at 0.5% risk is about 3%/yr at lab costs (audit CAGR 3.1-3.4%) and about 2%/yr with retail frictions.
issues.effect_on_results: Below about EUR 6-9k the backtest's sizing assumption fails. On a EUR 6-10k account the expected EUR 100-300 per year is close to the cost of a 24/5 VPS (about EUR 10-15 per month).

issues.description: Bars aligned on the MT5 server clock. The rule is only sensitive to the 4h bar grid at the margin, but the track report quotes the server-grid check from unpatched data; on patched data the MT5 server grid fails IS t>=2. The existing EA correctly builds UTC-grid bars, but a trader reading the native H4 chart sees different bars.
issues.evidence: p3_grid.out, IS / VAL PF: fixed UTC+0/+1/+2/+3 grids 1.350/1.349/1.284/1.304 and 1.294/1.256/1.264/1.354. NY-17:00 server grid (UTC+2/+3 with US DST) 1.279 (t 1.94, n 482) / 1.306. Athens-time grid (EU DST) 1.283 (t 1.97) / 1.298. 91% of UTC-grid IS trades have a same-side server-grid trade within 4h. trials.jsonl line 49 (unpatched) shows PF 1.313, t 2.12, n 474, which is the figure in report.md.
issues.effect_on_results: Using the native MT5 H4 bars is a slightly different rule (IS PF -0.07, t below 2). The UTC grid is the best or equal best of the 4 phases on IS, which points to mild phase luck.

issues.description: Time-stop parity bug in the EA. DeadlineUTC (line 141, called at line 457 with the bucket start) counts calendar weekdays from the start of the current 4h UTC bucket. The backtest instead uses the NY-17:00 trading-day convention from the previous bar's close time, minus 5 minutes, falling back to the last bar before a market closure.
issues.evidence: p6_ea_parity.out and p9_misc.out: 226 of 2646 brackets get a different time-stop bar. Trades entered at the Sunday open from the Friday-close bracket exit about 23h later; Sunday-evening decisions exit 50-54h earlier (Friday 16:55 NY instead of Sunday evening of the next week); Good Friday cases exit 73h later (the EA waits for the first tick after Easter). Re-simulating with the EA's deadlines gives IS 1.352 / VAL 1.294, with IS time exits 8 against 8 and the same IS maximum hold.
issues.effect_on_results: No measurable PF effect (time exits are rare), but it breaks trade-by-trade parity and can hold through holiday closures.

issues.description: Time-zone handling in the EA. GO_TZ_AUTO applies today's measured server offset to all 90 days of M5 history, and GO_TZ_FIXED applies one fixed offset, so both are wrong across a DST change. GO_TZ_NY_CLOSE assumes US DST dates, so on an EET (EU-DST) server it is 1 hour off for about 3 weeks a year. The offset is checked only once, in OnInit (line 598).
issues.evidence: Source: ServerOffsetSec lines 112-120 (the AUTO branch uses TimeTradeServer()-TimeGMT() for every bar); Build4H line 183 converts every M5 bar with that offset. The grid tests above show that a 1-hour grid shift gives IS PF 1.28-1.35 (p3_grid.out).
issues.effect_on_results: Small PF effect, but during the mismatch weeks the levels, deadlines and journal timestamps are off by 1 hour, which spoils parity checks.

issues.description: In auto mode (line 407), PlacePendings silently skips a side when the price is already at or beyond the level, or within StopsLevel, at the first tick. The backtest instead fills a gap through the level at the open. MT5 also refuses pending orders while the market is closed, so the Sunday bracket can only be armed after the gap has happened.
issues.evidence: p6_ea_parity.out: sides that cannot be placed at the first tick: 82 (StopsLevel $0), 275 ($0.5), 562 ($1), 1284 ($2). IS / VAL PF with those trades removed: 1.347 / 1.285, 1.338 / 1.281, 1.358 / 1.264, 1.240 / 1.214. 16 baseline trades (12 IS) fill on the bracket's first M1 bar, for +5.2 R in total.
issues.effect_on_results: Small for StopsLevel up to $1; IS falls to 1.24 at $2.

issues.description: Robustness gaps in the EA. (1) No deterministic replay after downtime, and the bracket state is not persisted: a breakout missed while offline, or a bracket re-armed mid-window after a restart, makes the fictive position diverge from the backtest. (2) No SERIES_SYNCHRONIZED or gap check on CopyRates; when history is short (line 425) the bracket is skipped for 4 hours with only a Print. (3) LotsForRisk (lines 308-324) falls back to the minimum lot even when that is several times the target risk, and auto mode trades it anyway. (4) The Telegram WebRequest is synchronous with a 5-second timeout inside OnTick (line 247). (5) OnNewM1 (line 491) processes only the last closed M1 bar, so trailing updates are lost after a disconnection. (6) Mode 1 manages any magic-0 position on the same side, with no ticket binding. (7) The 0.25 ATR pre-alert gives too little warning.
issues.evidence: Source lines cited. p9_misc.out: pre-alert lead before the trigger at 0.25 ATR has median 5 min (47% under 5 min); at 0.5 ATR, median 24 min (24% under 5 min). p5_sizing.out shows effective risk up to 5% under the minimum-lot fallback.
issues.effect_on_results: Silent divergence between the EA journal and the backtest, and accidental over-risking on small accounts. These undermine the planned phase-2 comparison of real results against the backtest.

issues.description: Pending orders placed by hand at the 4h closes inside waking hours, and left in place overnight, keep the IS edge and leave VAL only modestly lower. This is the only manual mode tested that does so. These variants were built after VAL and are informational only.
issues.evidence: p2_availability.out and p8_combos.out. Pending orders refreshed only at in-window 4h closes, GTC overnight with stale levels, EA trailing: W1 IS 1.359 (t 2.38) / VAL 1.255; W2 1.381 (t 2.48) / 1.233. Same with the SL moved by hand at those checks: W1 1.309 (t 2.08) / 1.182; W2 1.347 (t 2.25) / 1.180. Risk of both pending orders filling (MT5 has no OCO): the opposite level was touched before the next check in 0 of 490 IS trades.
issues.effect_on_results: Gives a practical 'he decides' mode that roughly preserves the IS edge (VAL 1.18-1.26), provided the trader places stops rather than chasing at market.

issues.description: EA level construction from M5 bid plus spread/2 matches the backtest's mid-price levels. Weekend gap exposure is modest.
issues.evidence: p6_ea_parity.out. EA-style channel minus backtest channel: high median $0.00 (p5 -0.09, p95 +0.07); low median $0.00 (p5 -0.20, p95 +0.07). PF with EA-style levels: IS 1.381-1.382 / VAL 1.294-1.307. 109 of 499 IS trades are held over a weekend; 3 exit at the post-weekend gap (R -1.50, -0.78, -0.87); the worst IS R is -1.50.
issues.effect_on_results: None material.

recommendations: EXECUTION MODE. Never enter at market from a trigger alert: a 1-minute delay already gives IS PF 1.24-1.26 with t<2. The manual version that survives uses pending orders. At each 4h close inside waking hours (08/12/16/20 UTC, i.e. 09/13/17/21h Paris in winter and 10/14/18/22h in summer), if flat, place BOTH a buy-stop and a sell-stop at the alerted levels, each with its SL attached at level -/+ 2 ATR, as GTC orders. Leave them until the next check, and delete the other order as soon as one fills. This gives IS 1.36 / VAL 1.26 with EA trailing, or 1.31 / 1.18 with the SL moved by hand at the same checks. These are post-VAL variants and informational only. If a trigger alert arrives and no pending order was in place, skip the trade.

EXITS. Run the EA on a 24/5 VPS that pushes the server-side SL to best price -/+ 2 ATR at every M1 close (mode 1 for manual positions, mode 2 later), bound to a specific ticket. Do not use MT5's built-in trailing (client-side, starts only at +2 ATR, IS PF 1.205), and do not rely on phone-only SL updates (IS 1.18 / VAL 1.05).

ACCOUNT AND SIZING. Read SYMBOL_TRADE_CONTRACT_SIZE, VOLUME_MIN and VOLUME_STEP at the broker. With 100-oz lots, 0.5% risk needs at least about EUR 6.0k (2025 median stop $35/oz) and about EUR 9.4k at Q4-2025 volatility ($55/oz); 1% risk needs half that. Below this, do not trade, or accept 1% risk. The EA should block, or ask for confirmation, whenever the minimum lot implies more than 1.5x the target risk. Expect about 3%/yr at 0.5% risk under lab costs and about 2%/yr under retail frictions, with max drawdown around 8-10 R. Compare that with the VPS cost (about EUR 10-15 per month) before going live.

BROKER DUE DILIGENCE BEFORE ANY REAL MONEY (EA journal, at least 3 weeks). Log the spread every minute from 16:45 to 18:30 NY; StopsLevel, FreezeLevel and allowed expiration modes; digits; long and short swap and the triple-swap day; the server UTC offset and whether DST follows US or EU dates; and, on demo, stop-order slippage and latency. Re-run the lab with these numbers (scripts in the scratch folder). Each extra bp of slippage per side costs 0.023 R per trade, and a x5 pre-close spread spike cuts IS PF to 1.09.

HOLDOUT. Keep the single 2026 look on the unchanged rule. Before downloading 2026, pre-declare and then report beside it, as information only, these as-executed variants: EA auto with retail frictions (3 bp, swaps 8/3); pending orders while awake with EA trailing; the same with hand-moved SL; market entry 5 min late; and the NY-17:00 server grid. Never use them to pick or retune the rule.

EA SPEC, PHASE 1 (alert-only, always-on VPS). (1) Bars: build UTC-grid 4h mid-price bars from M1, at least 30 trading days back. Check SERIES_SYNCHRONIZED and the bar count, and look for unexplained gaps over 15 min in the 60-bar window. If anything is wrong, send a DATA_WARN alert and arm no bracket; retry for the first 10 minutes. (2) Clock: convert server time to UTC with a per-bar offset from a selectable DST rule (US NY-close, EU/EET, or fixed). Re-check it at every 4h close against TimeTradeServer()-TimeGMT(), and alert on mismatch. (3) Decision: at each 4h close (the bar's last M1 + 1 min), if the fictive position is flat, compute the 60-bar mid high and low (including the just-closed bar), Wilder ATR14, and stop = trail = 2 ATR. Compute the deadline exactly as the lab does: NY time + 7h, + BDay(5), - 7h, - 5 min, falling back to the last bar before a closure. (4) Fictive fills: ask >= buy level or bid <= sell level, at max(level, quote) so a gap fills at the open; per-M1 trailing from the best bid-high or ask-low; time stop; if both levels are touched in the same minute, take the adverse side. (5) On startup, replay M1 history since the last saved state to rebuild the fictive position and brackets, tag those events REPLAY, and never arm a bracket mid-window unless the replay shows the fictive position was flat at that window's start. (6) Send notifications outside OnTick (Telegram asynchronously), with a daily heartbeat and a weekly summary.

(c) PlacePendings (line 407): if the level is already crossed at arming, send a market order (as the backtest's gap fill does), and alert if a side cannot be placed because of StopsLevel. MT5 PITFALLS FOR THIS RULE. (1) Pending orders: ORDER_TIME_SPECIFIED only works if SYMBOL_EXPIRATION_MODE allows it, and expiry is in server time. Pending orders are refused while the market is closed (weekend and the 17:00-18:00 NY break), so the Sunday bracket is armed after the gap. MT5 has no OCO: delete the other order on DEAL_ENTRY_IN, and know whether the account is hedging or netting. (2) StopsLevel and FreezeLevel: pending orders closer than StopsLevel are rejected, and SL changes inside FreezeLevel are refused, so retry each minute and never move the SL further away. (3) Weekend and holiday gaps: the SL and the pending stops fill at the first price after the gap; 22% of trades are held over a weekend and losses can exceed 1 R (worst IS -1.50 R). (4) Trailing: EA-managed server-side SL, not terminal trailing (client-side, starts at +2 ATR, missing from the mobile app). (5) H4 timestamps: native H4 bars follow server time (NY-17:00 grid), a different rule (IS t 1.94), so never read levels off the native chart; the EA must build UTC bars. (6) Partial data at startup: history may still be syncing, the 'Max bars in chart' setting may cap it, or there may be gaps after a disconnection, so check before arming. (7) DST: the UTC grid itself does not move, but the server offset changes; US and EU DST dates differ for 2-3 weeks in March and 1 week in October/November, and the 17:00 NY rollover moves between 21:00 and 22:00 UTC. (8) Rollover: retail spread spikes are larger than in Dukascopy data; measure them. (9) Symbol specifics: contract size (100 oz or 1 oz), 2 or 3 digits, suffixes, tick value in EUR. (10) Notifications: push needs the MetaQuotes ID and is limited to about 2 per second and 10 per minute; Alert() popups are not seen on a VPS; Telegram needs the URL whitelisted.

PARITY PROCEDURE. Run the MT5 tester in 'Every tick based on real ticks' mode on 2025 with InpServerTZ = NY_CLOSE (AUTO is disabled in the tester), then lab/live/compare_journal.py. Add a bracket-level check: levels within $0.5 and ATR within 2% of the lab. During phase 1, compare each week the EA's fictive trades with a lab re-run on Dukascopy data, and the real fills with the fictive ones (slippage, latency). Any persistent difference above 0.03 R per trade is material, since the edge is about 0.10 R.

A deliberate 1-5-bar look-ahead does not raise PF. My own end-to-end check (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-gold-orb/340d9f5a-4d28-5733-90cb-10a10699d00b/scratchpad/judge_causality.py, IS only): with all prices garbled after 5 cut dates (2014-2021), every trade closed before the cut is bit-identical (66/66 up to 469/469) through make_orders, simulate and the one-position chain. Implementable. An MT5 EA on a 24/5 VPS reproduces the exact rule: UTC-grid bars built from M1, cancel-on-fill OCO, and a server-side SL moved at each M1 close (median 18, p90 67 modifications per trade). ESMA 1:20 margin is not binding. Alert/manual execution failing, and the minimum lot setting an account floor, are deployment constraints, not an impossibility.

Low conviction even so. Selection-adjusted IS p is about 0.14-0.15 (Reality Check / SPA). VAL every-signal PF is 0.977. VAL profit is all long (+34.4 R against -9.7 R on shorts), and 64% of it is from 2025. Read the holdout against bands declared in advance; a PF > 1 alone does not justify real money.
judge.p_edge_real: About 0.30 (plausible 0.20-0.40) that the rule, executed exactly by an EA, has positive expectancy after the pre-registered costs going forward. About 0.10 that the edge is as large as measured (>= +0.10 R/trade, PF >= 1.3). If it is real, the likely size is +0.03 to +0.06 R/trade (PF about 1.08-1.15). That is small enough for 1-2 bp/side of extra slippage, broker rollover spikes or manual entry to erase it. For alert-driven manual market entries, below 0.15. Basis: strong IS evidence against random-timing nulls (beats all 1000 runs, 3.7 sd), offset by search selection (best of 48, N_eff about 21, RC p 0.15), a VAL signal-level null (every-signal PF 0.977, below the drift-kept null median of 1.083), long-only VAL profit, and weak cross-market support (VAL mean PF about 0.97).
judge.expected_holdout: The holdout runs from 2026-01-01 to early Nov 2026: about 10 months and 45-55 trades. Blended forecast: PF median about 1.0, 90% range about 0.4-2.2, and P(PF > 1, the protocol pass) about 0.45-0.50, close to a coin flip. Reference cases: with the edge as measured, median 1.30 [0.55, 2.79] and P(PF > 1) 0.70; with half the edge, 1.12 and 0.59; with no edge, 0.87-0.97 [0.35-0.39, 1.9-2.1] and 0.39-0.47. Expect an 8-11 R max drawdown, about one week in three positive, a result decided by 2-4 large trend trades, and a long/short split that follows gold's 2026 direction. Reading declared in advance, starting from 0.30: PF >= 1.5 is weak support (to about 0.5); 1.0-1.5 is a protocol pass but inconclusive (about 0.4); 0.8-1.0 is mild evidence against (about 0.25); below 0.7 is meaningful evidence against (about 0.12). A profit made only on longs while gold rises counts for nothing. Report alongside it, as information only: every-signal PF, the long/short split, and same-period 2026 nulls (signal times with random side; random long-only and short-only entries with identical exits). Also report the as-executed variants: the EA with 3 bp slippage and 8%/3% swaps; hand-placed pending stops with EA trailing; 5-min market entry; and the NY-17 server grid.
judge.manual_trading_viable: No, not as 'alert, then decide, then market order'. That is a weaker strategy that fails the IS t >= 2 criterion at any delay. Late market entry, IS PF / VAL PF: 1 min 1.24-1.26 (t 1.73-1.80) / 1.26; 5 min 1.23-1.24 / 1.17-1.20; 15 min 1.18-1.22 / 1.10-1.12; 60 min 1.11-1.14 / 1.12-1.19. Chasing costs +0.03 to +0.05 R/trade against an edge of about 0.12 R, and the loss falls on the fastest winners. Availability makes it worse. Waking hours only (07-23 Paris) with instant fills: IS 1.313 (t 1.94) / VAL 1.117; with 5-min entries: 1.203 / 1.028. Night triggers are 15% of IS trades but carry 24% of IS R and 65% of VAL R. Mon-Fri 08-20 Paris with 5-min entries: 1.146 / 1.173. Exits fail too: MT5 terminal trailing gives IS 1.205 (t 1.54). Phone-only SL management gives 1.178 / 1.050, and 1.050 / 0.930 with retail frictions. Only one semi-manual mode holds up. At each waking-hours 4h close the trader places BOTH resting stop orders (GTC, SL attached) and leaves them overnight, while a VPS EA cancels the other order on fill and trails per M1. That gives IS 1.36-1.38 (t 2.38-2.48) / VAL 1.23-1.26, or 1.31-1.35 / 1.18 with the SL moved by hand. These variants were built after VAL and are not validated. Use alerts only for the journal and paper tracking. Execute through resting broker-side orders with a VPS EA; fully automated is preferred.
ea_spec: Execution: a fully automated MT5 EA on a 24/5 VPS, XAUUSD, one position at a time, with resting broker-side orders and a server-side SL. The Phase 1 alert mode tracks the fictive position as the forward paper record; run a demo-auto copy in parallel to measure real fills.

Bars and clock: 4h mid bars on the fixed UTC grid (00/04/08/12/16/20), built from broker M1 (or M5) bid + spread/2. Never use the native H4 chart: its NY-17 server grid gives IS 1.279, t 1.94. Convert server time to UTC with a per-bar DST rule (US NY-close, EU/EET or fixed), and re-check it against TimeTradeServer()-TimeGMT() at every 4h close; on a mismatch send OFFSET_WARN and arm no bracket. Keep at least 640 4h bars of history so the ATR matches the lab exactly.

Decision: at each 4h close, only if flat at that moment. up = max mid-high and dn = min mid-low over the last 60 completed 4h bars, INCLUDING the bar just closed. ATR = Wilder ATR14 on mid 4h bars (alpha 1/14, TR uses the previous mid close). D = 2.0 x ATR, frozen for the trade. Excluding the current bar or using stale levels costs 0.06-0.08 IS PF.

Entry: BuyStop at up (triggers on ask) and SellStop at dn (triggers on bid), each with an attached SL at level -/+ D, valid until the next 4h close; delete it at the next decision. OCO: on DEAL_ENTRY_IN, delete the other order; if both fill, close the second at once. If price is already through a level when arming (gap, Sunday open), enter at market, matching the backtest's fill at the open. If StopsLevel blocks a side, log and alert. After the fill, reset the SL to fill -/+ D.

Trailing: at each M1 close, best = highest bid-high (long) or lowest ask-low (short) since the fill, including the M1 bar just closed. Set SL = best -/+ D whenever that tightens it, send it to the server, and never loosen it. Process every M1 bar missed after a disconnect. When StopsLevel or FreezeLevel blocks a change, retry each minute. Do not use MT5 terminal trailing (IS 1.205) or OnTick trailing.

Time stop: close at market at the decision's NY wall-clock time + 5 NY business days - 5 min. The lab computes this as NY time + 7h, + BDay(5), - 7h, - 5 min. If that time falls in a closure (weekend, holiday or early close, with the next quote more than 30 min later), close on the last bar before it. Fix DeadlineUTC (lines 141/457) to match.

Sizing: lots = floor(equity x risk% / loss-per-lot at D / VOLUME_STEP) x VOLUME_STEP, with risk at 0.25-0.5%. Block, or ask for confirmation, when VOLUME_MIN would mean more than 1.5x the target risk. With 100-oz lots, 0.5% risk needs at least EUR 6.0k at the 2025 median stop ($35/oz) and EUR 9.4k at Q4-2025 volatility ($55/oz). Never skip signals at discretion.

Resilience: persist the bracket and position state. On restart, replay M1 since the last save (tagged REPLAY), and never arm mid-window unless the replay shows the position was flat at that window's start. Check SERIES_SYNCHRONIZED, the bar count and any gap over 15 min in the 60-bar window; on failure send DATA_WARN, arm no bracket and retry for 10 min. Bind management to the position ticket. Keep WebRequest/Telegram out of OnTick. Send a daily heartbeat. Replace the 0.25-ATR pre-alert (median lead 5 min) with a NIVEAUX alert at each 4h close.

Journal: a CSV with one row per event. Fields: UTC, Paris and server time; offset used vs measured; event type (LEVELS, TRIGGER, SL_MOVE, EXIT, REAL_FILL, REAL_SL_MOD, REAL_CLOSE, DATA_WARN, OFFSET_WARN, REPLAY, DISCONNECT, HEARTBEAT); levels; ATR; fictive vs real price; slippage; latency; spread. Also log the spread every minute from 16:45 to 18:30 NY, and compare fictive R with a lab re-run every week.

Gates before real money: run the MT5 tester in 'every tick based on real ticks' mode on 2025, then compare_journal.py; require levels within $0.5, ATR within 2% and at least 90% of trades matched. Then run at least 3 weeks of demo to measure the rollover and pre-close spread, stop slippage, swaps and StopsLevel/FreezeLevel. A x5 pre-close spike cuts IS PF to 1.07-1.09. Keep slippage at or below about 1.5 bp/side; at 3 bp, IS falls to 1.23 (t 1.66). Treat a persistent real-vs-fictive gap above 0.03 R/trade as material.
open_risks: Selection: the candidate is the best of 48 correlated trend configs (N_eff about 21). White Reality Check p is 0.151 and SPA p is 0.138. The audit's DSR of 0.07 is mis-specified; recomputed, it ranges from 0.09 to 0.69 depending on assumptions.

VAL is weak evidence. Every-signal VAL PF is 0.977. The chain passes only because the signals it took beat the ones it skipped: +0.147 R in VAL (98th percentile of the null) against -0.003 R in IS. A drift-only null passes the VAL test 48% of the time. Data patching alone moved VAL PF from 1.232 to 1.294.

Concentration: the top 5% of trades make 145-150% of net R. Removing 15 IS trades or 7 VAL trades wipes out net R. PF without the top 10 trades: IS 1.08, VAL 0.91. IS t drops below 2 without 2020 or without 2016.
Regime and beta: since 2017 the profit has come from longs in a rising gold market (shorts -21.2 R over 222 trades in 2017-25). A long-only profit in 2026 cannot be told apart from beta.

Holdout power: about 50 trades. P(PF > 1) is 0.70 if the edge is as measured and 0.39-0.47 if there is none, so no 10-month outcome settles it. Confirming the edge would take roughly 600-2300 trades. A pass should lead to sequential demo monitoring with a kill rule fixed in advance (for example cumulative R <= -10 or posterior < 0.15), not to real money.

Execution fragility: each extra bp/side of slippage costs about 0.023 R/trade against an edge of about 0.10 R. Each extra 10% of trigger-bar overshoot costs about 0.06 PF, and the tick calibration rests on only 25 trades. A x5 pre-close broker spread spike cuts IS PF to 1.07-1.09. The MT5 server grid, an off-by-one channel or terminal trailing each push IS t below 2.

Small-account economics: a 0.01-lot trade risks the full 2-ATR stop, $35-55/oz in 2025. Expect about 2-3%/yr at 0.5% risk, which is roughly the VPS cost on a EUR 6-10k account. Expect 8-11 R drawdowns; weekend gaps can lose more than 1 R (worst -1.5 R).

Holdout process: lab/holdout_candidates.json does not exist yet and must be frozen before get_holdout.sh runs. It needs trend/donch4h_stop, the FINALISTS params, a 'prereg': {} cost key (holdout.py reads that key for the pass flag), the three COSTS.md scenarios, the reading bands and the as-executed variants. Keep the 2026 hole-patching. Warm-start from full history, or check that the 2025-06 warm start reproduces the audited Dec-2025 chain, so the short still open on 2025-12-31 carries into 2026. Flag the trade still open at the end of the data, which is marked to market as 'time'.

Forking paths: do not adopt any fix the diagnostics suggest (long-only, a low-ATR filter, first-breakout-only, session or grid changes). Each of them has seen VAL; register them only as new hypotheses for forward data.

The existing EA (lab/live/mql5/GoldOrb_Donchian4H.mq5) is not ready for parity testing. DeadlineUTC uses a different deadline convention and ignores holidays. DST uses a single offset: AUTO and FIXED are wrong across DST changes, NY_CLOSE is 1 h off on EET servers about 3 weeks a year, and the offset is checked only in OnInit. PlacePendings silently skips sides that are gapped through or too close. The bracket is not persisted and there is no replay after downtime. A CopyRates failure silently skips the 4h bracket. LotsForRisk falls back to the minimum lot even when that over-risks. OnNewM1 processes only the last M1 bar. Mode 1 manages any magic-0 position on the same side. WebRequest runs synchronously inside OnTick.

issues.description: Engine/strategy interaction: Costs.spread_mult is applied inside simulate() to quotes that differ from the quotes make_orders used to pre-resolve the OCO first touch. Those orders have entry_i = expiry_i = the touch bar, a one-bar window. With spread_mult < 1, the lowered Ask or raised Bid on the touch bar may no longer reach the level. The order then NOFILLs silently and the day is lost, with no later touch and no earlier one. With spread_mult > 1, fills stay forced on the old bar and the levels are not widened, so the result is optimistic. audit.py scenarios and holdout.py both apply Costs(**c) to the normal-quote orders. The low_cost_ecn scenario (spread_mult 0.35) is what decides CONDITIONAL under Amendment 1, so it is computed on the wrong trade list.

issues.description: Under the primary model the pass/fail call sits inside the execution and feed noise band. Cent-level feed noise and 1-minute timing shifts move PF by about ±0.02-0.03, which is the size of the IS gap to 1.20. VAL PF 1.1002 clears the 1.10 bar by 0.0002, so criterion 7 is effectively a coin flip under small execution differences.

issues.description: Intrabar fill fidelity: stop entries and stop exits fill at exactly the level, plus 1.5 bp. A tick replay of Jun-Dec 2025 shows the real trigger tick jumps past the level. This is covered by the primary slippage budget, but it uses up more than half of the low_cost_ecn budget (0.75 bp per side).

Mean adverse entry jump is $0.175 (median 0.078, p90 0.414) and mean exit jump $0.120, against a 2x1.5 bp budget of $1.105 per trade. The R gap is 0.0076 R per trade (PF 1.234 M1 vs 1.218 tick, with the same costs on both). The bound for filling at the touch-minute close is IS PF 1.132 (p6 variant B).
issues.effect_on_results: About -0.015 PF if slippage were zero. Under the primary costs there is no net bias. Under low_cost_ecn the effective cushion is about $0.25 per trade.

issues.description: The time exit uses pd.offsets.BDay(2), which ignores holidays. When 16:00 NY falls in a closed market (US holidays, early closes, Good Friday, Christmas, Thanksgiving), the exit happens at the reopen, 2 to 51 hours late. The longest IS hold is 159 h: entry 2013-12-20, exit 2013-12-27 00:00 UTC. That is still within 5 trading days. The engine charges swap for the extra nights.
issues.evidence: p7_holes_holidays.out: 19 IS time exits came more than 30 min after schedule, summing to +30.9 R. Closing at the last quote before the scheduled time would give +28.5 R. The hand check of trade 205 (p4_handcheck.out) shows 7 swap nights.
issues.effect_on_results: -2.4 R over IS if the EA closes before early closes, about -0.003 PF. The EA convention needs to be documented.

issues.description:
Holdout pipeline data prep differs from the IS/VAL prep.
- holdout.py only re-downloads days with fewer than 50% of the median bar count, so partial-day holes stay unpatched. The patch changed IS PF by -0.019 (issue 1).
- build() skips prep_data's crossed-quote filter (ask < bid, or ask_low < bid_low - 5).
- Cost scenarios reuse the normal-quote orders (issue 2).
The warm-up frame itself is fine: starting at 2025-06-01 gives identical orders, and the trade path re-converges within 3 days.
issues.evidence: lab/holdout.py build() / short_days() / main(). p19_holdout_frame.out: orders identical; only 2025-06-02/03/05 trades differ (warm-up). p15_remaining_holes.out: the current IS/VAL data has only holiday short days and 30 unexpected gaps of 15 min or more over 13 years.
issues.effect_on_results: An unpatched 2026 file with holes biased the same way as before could move the single-look PF by about 0.02. It cannot be redone after the look.

issues.description: A few entries were triggered by Dukascopy spread spikes: the triggering Ask high or Bid low came with 3x or more the prior-hour median spread. Their outcome depends on the feed. A broker feed without the same spike would not have taken them.

issues.effect_on_results: About -0.012 PF if the 3x-or-more spike entries were absent.

issues.description:
No look-ahead in strategy.py or goldlab: every decision uses only completed bars before the decision.
- The range is built from bars starting 00:00-06:59 London (ask high / bid low), and orders are live from the first bar starting at or after 07:00.
- The first touch is scanned forward causally. The both-levels-in-one-bar tie never occurs in IS.
- The 4 gap fills are taken at the worse of level and open. The stop check on the fill bar is pessimistic.
- There are no whole-series statistics. Daily ATR and trend are computed but unused, and orders do not change under truncation.
- M1 bars are start-labelled. DST is handled for London and NY, including the mismatch weeks.
issues.evidence:
p5_truncation.out, 150 random IS sessions:
- data ending at the touch bar gives an identical order 150/150
- data ending one bar earlier gives no order 150/150
- data ending at 06:59 London gives no order 150/150
- 6/6 full-history cuts are identical
- the 14 'previous orders' mismatches are a window-start artefact (p5b_prevcheck.out)
p3_ea_replica.out: an independent bar-by-bar EA written from the report rules gives IS 1037/1037 and VAL 445/445 trades, max |dR| 0, identical swaps. p4_handcheck.out: 16 trades (12 random plus the longest hold, a Friday entry, the max R and the min risk) match raw M1 rows to 1e-6. p2_timestamps.out: tick-to-M1 aggregation is 100% exact with start labels and about 1-2% with end labels. p2c_sessions.out: range start is 00:00 UTC in winter and 23:00 UTC in BST; the exit is 21:00 / 20:00 UTC.
issues.effect_on_results: None. The backtest is what an EA following the stated rules would have done on this feed.

issues.description: Decision-time and fill-timing shifts degrade results smoothly, with no cliff. Entering by alert at market 1-60 minutes after the touch keeps most of the result. The apparent collapse at +60 minutes (IS PF 0.847) is an R-normalisation artefact: one entry landed $0.004 from the stop, giving R = -217.

p6_delay.out:
- arming +1/+5/+15 bars: PF 1.175 / 1.170 / 1.195
- range_end 06:59 / 07:01 / 07:05: PF 1.180 / 1.158 / 1.156
- VAL for market entries at k=1..60 bars: PF 1.089-1.101

issues.effect_on_results: For alert mode: -0.01 to -0.02 PF for a 1-30 minute manual delay, provided a 'skip if price has already moved halfway to the stop' rule is used.

issues.description:
Other fidelity points checked, all negligible:
- Data holes remaining inside holds.
- prep_data._drop_flat removing flat-bid minutes, which also drops their ask information.
- Rollover and reopen spread blow-outs at retail brokers.
- The broker stops-level for pending orders.
The high PF of 'trades containing a hole' is a hold-length effect, not hidden stop-outs.
issues.evidence: p7b_holes_detail.out: 87 IS holds contain unexpected gaps of 5 min or more. Only 1 trade (2019-02-26, +2.62R) had price within 0.25R of the stop at a hole edge. Mean R of time exits is 2.36 with a hole vs 2.04 without; holds average 78 h vs 39 h. p10_dropflat.out: dropped minutes raised the range high on 2 days by at most $0.10, caused 0 earlier buy triggers and 0 hidden short stops. p9_rollover.out: spread x3 / +$1 / +$2 in 16:55-18:30 NY gives PF 1.172 / 1.174 / 1.165. p16 (p16_swap_stopslevel.out): the nearer level is within $0.5 of the 07:00 quote in 1.9% of sessions.
issues.effect_on_results: Each between 0 and -0.012 PF. The worst case from a hidden stop is -0.006.

issues.description: The swap model (a fixed 5% / 2% per year) matters for a strategy held about 1.4 nights on average. Real gold swaps move with USD rates, so this is a period-dependent error rather than a fixed one.
issues.evidence:
p16_swap_stopslevel.out: swap costs 0.025 R per trade.
- zero swap: PF 1.217
- long 8% / short 0%: 1.172
- long 8% / short 3%: 1.155
- long 10% / short 5%: 1.133

reviews.verdict: Not pure luck: breakout direction carries real gross information (VAL z 1.8-1.9 against permutation nulls). But the net edge is about 0 ± 0.06 R/trade once selection, year effects and path dependence are counted. Best estimate P(net edge > 0) ≈ 0.4 and P(≥ +0.05 R/trade) ≈ 0.15. The VAL pass is knife-edge (PF 1.1002), and a 10-month holdout cannot tell H1 from H0 (likelihood ratio ≤ 2 for pass/fail).

issues.description: Once selection is counted, the IS result is what you would expect if the net edge were zero. Under a zero-net null (true expectancy exactly 0, all trials), the best of the ORB track's correlated configs reaches the candidate's IS t of 1.83 about half the time. Project-wide, one 'IS near-pass + VAL pass' candidate appearing by luck is a coin flip.
issues.evidence: s03: the weekly-R correlation matrix of the 48 re-simulated ORB configs gives M_eff = 23 (Li-Ji) / 24.9 (Galwey) / 40 (Nyholt). Stages 1-4 give 20-22 of 31; the Asia multi-day sub-family gives 9-10 of 26. Correlated-normal simulation of the max t under the zero-net null: P(max ≥ 1.83) = 0.48 (all 48), 0.46 (stages 1-4), 0.21 (Asia sub-family). Week-block centred bootstrap: P(IS ≥ candidate level) = 2.9% and P(VAL pass) = 21.6% per trial. P(≥1 of N_eff reaches the candidate's IS level): N=10 0.26, N=23 0.50, N=48 0.76, N=100 0.95, N=321/370 ≈ 1.0. Project level (best config per track, one VAL shot each, 6 tracks): P(≥1 track yields IS ≥ this level and passes VAL) ≈ 0.50. Corrected deflated Sharpe (noise variance 1/T): 0.44 (N=23), 0.32 (N=48), 0.12 (N=321). The audit's DSR of 0.0012 overstates the penalty, because the cross-trial SR variance it uses includes real cost differences between configs. Empirical Bayes over the project's 6 finalists' VAL t (-1.84, 0.74, -0.92, -0.79, -1.53, 1.49; mean -0.48) shrinks this candidate to +0.003 R/trade, P(>0) = 0.52.
issues.effect_on_results: The IS near-pass (and the unpatched 1.196/1.99) carries a Bayes factor of about 1 against 'gross edge just equals cost'. Nearly all the selection-free evidence is the single VAL look, which is weak (t 0.74).

issues.description: The VAL pass is knife-edge and fragile. On the current (patched) data the VAL PF is 1.1002 against the 1.10 threshold. Small, equally valid changes in execution or path push it below 1.10. The VAL bar also cannot tell a breakout edge from long drift: in the 2022-2025 bull market a random-time always-long rule with the same structure passes it most of the time.
issues.evidence: s01: VAL n 445, PF 1.10018 unrounded, t 0.742 (gl.report rounds it to 1.1). Week-block bootstrap: P(VAL PF ≥ 1.10) = 49.5%, P(exp ≤ 0) = 21.6%, 90% CI 0.90-1.33. Entering at market one minute after the touch (C1) gives VAL PF 1.080. Randomly missing 5%/10%/20%/33% of signals (500 seeds each) gives VAL median PF 1.084/1.077/1.060/1.030, with P(VAL ≥ 1.10) = 36%/33%/28%/23%. Always long at the candidate's signal times (L1): VAL PF 1.135, passes. Random-time always-long (N2L, 333 seeds): VAL median PF 1.123, 63% pass. The candidate's VAL profit is all longs (+33.4 R; shorts -4.4 R).
issues.effect_on_results: Criterion 7 gives about no evidence (VAL Bayes factor 1.14-1.31 for an edge of 0.06-0.10 vs 0). A live alert-follower who misses a few signals should expect a VAL-like PF of about 1.06-1.08, i.e. a fail.

issues.description: Year and regime dependence, plus concentration. Profit comes from a few trend years and a handful of trades. Which side earns follows each year's drift. The iid per-trade t overstates the evidence once between-year heterogeneity is modelled.
issues.evidence: s04, random effects over years (DerSimonian-Laird): tau = 0.17 R/trade (IS, Q p = 0.058, I² 0.47) and 0.13 (IS+VAL). RE mean 0.069 ± 0.062 (t 1.12, IS+VAL); IS alone t 0.88 (vs iid 1.83). 2013 gives 86.8 of 124.3 IS R. Without 2013: IS PF 1.059 (t 0.62), IS+VAL PF 1.072 (t 0.92). The top 1% of IS trades = 89% of IS R; dropping the top 10 IS trades gives PF 1.02. In VAL the top 4 trades = 132% of VAL R; dropping the top 5 gives PF 0.94. IS top 10 weeks = 98% of R; VAL top 5 weeks = 135%. Short minus long: IS +0.185 (t 1.41), VAL -0.161 (t -0.91). corr(yearly long-minus-short R, gold annual return) = 0.78. Spearman(yearly total R, |gold return|) = 0.62. Losing years (2018, 2021, 2022) are range years; 2013, 2020, 2024 and 2025 (|ret| ≥ 20%) had PF 1.26-2.43. Regime splits reverse between IS and VAL: high-vol PF 0.80 vs 1.17; choppy (ER20) 1.39 vs 0.96; 20-day-trend-aligned 1.12 vs 1.15 with counter-trend 1.24 vs 1.06. No stable conditioning variable.
issues.effect_on_results: The edge behaves like trend-year exposure: positive in years with large gold moves, negative in range years. Its persistence depends on the regime, and a new year's mean R has a predictive SD of about 0.25 R/trade at ~95 trades.

issues.description: Path dependence of the one-position-at-a-time result. The headline PF depends on which signals no_overlap happens to skip. Variants that keep the same entries but change the path are near breakeven. Most 'robust' neighbours re-measure the same trades.
issues.evidence: Every signal traded (overlap allowed): IS PF 1.049 (t 0.71), VAL 1.012 (t 0.12). Taken vs skipped signals: IS +0.120 vs -0.078 R/trade (t 2.02), VAL +0.065 vs -0.064 (t 0.93). Random 5-33% dropout lowers the IS median PF steadily, 1.168 to 1.124, VAL 1.084 to 1.030. Hold 1 or 3 days: PF 1.044 / 1.023 (weekly-R corr with F3 0.57 / 0.54). 11 of the 14 stage-5 neighbours have corr ≥ 0.85 with F3. Neighbours with corr ≥ 0.9: median PF 1.162; corr < 0.8: 1.084; Spearman(neighbour PF, corr) = 0.63. Data version (s08): patching the data holes changed 33 of ~1030 IS trades (21 new ones sum to -10.0 R) and moved IS t from 1.99 to 1.83, PF from 1.196 to 1.177, years positive from 7/9 to 6/9. Every frictionless re-run takes a different path, so the per-config 'gross' differs by up to 0.15 R/trade between near-identical configs (F3 0.18 vs N02 0.33).
issues.effect_on_results: The neighbour criterion (median 1.159) gives little independent support. The path-free estimate of the signal's net value is about +0.01 to +0.035 R/trade, not +0.065 to +0.12.

issues.description: The CONDITIONAL status rests on a low-cost scenario that does not exist on disk. The amendment that created that status came after this candidate's near-miss. The scenario machinery in audit.py and holdout.py (spread_mult applied inside simulate to orders built with the original quotes) silently drops fills for this strategy, because each pending order is live only on its pre-computed touch bar (expiry_i = entry_i).
issues.evidence: No lab/COSTS.md and no lab/audit/cost_scenarios.json exist, and the audit's 'scenarios' block is {}. Amendment 1 is dated after the ORB report. s06, consistent method (spread scaled in the M1 frame before make_orders, then commission/slippage scaled): all costs x0.75 gives IS PF 1.232 (t 2.30), VAL 1.147 (t 1.06). Commission+slippage x0.5 only: IS 1.238 (t 2.36), VAL 1.151 (t 1.08). All x0.5: IS 1.293 (t 2.79), VAL 1.191 (t 1.33). Naive method at x0.75: 179 NOFILLs (7%), IS n 949, PF 1.183 (t 1.78, fails IS), VAL PF 1.006 (fails VAL).
issues.effect_on_results: Depending on implementation, the status flips between CONDITIONAL and FAIL. Even when consistent, lower costs only shift the mean by about 0.035 R/trade; the VAL t stays at about 1.1 and the selection problem is unchanged.

issues.description: A ~10-month 2026 holdout (~96 trades) has almost no power. Contrary to the protocol's note that 'a clear failure = strong information', even a bad holdout only halves the odds, and its reading is driven by gold's 2026 regime.
issues.evidence: s07, rolling 10-month windows 2013-2025. H1 as measured (mean +0.103 R): median PF 1.11, 90% range 0.71-1.61, P(PF>1) = 0.63. H1 shrunk to +0.05: median 1.04, P = 0.54. H0 zero-net: median 0.97, 0.61-1.39, P = 0.46. H0 random entry (N1/N2): median 0.87-0.88, 0.53-1.37, P = 0.30-0.32. Likelihood ratio for a pass (PF>1): 1.37 vs zero-net, 1.98-2.10 vs random. LR for a fail: 0.68 / 0.53. PF ≥ 1.4: LR 3.7-4.8. PF < 0.8: LR 0.37-0.51 (happens in 14% of H1 windows). Rejecting zero-net at 5% needs PF ≥ 1.39, with 18% power. s10: in windows where gold moved ≥ 15%, P(PF>1) = 0.80 under H1 and 0.64 even under zero-net; in flat windows (< 5%), 0.53 vs 0.37. 80% power against zero needs about 2,400 trades (~21 years).
issues.effect_on_results: From a 30% prior, a pass moves P(H1) to 0.37-0.46 and a fail to 0.19-0.23. Only PF ≥ ~1.4, or PF < ~0.8 (especially in a big-trend year), is informative.

issues.description: Pure luck from random entries is not a viable explanation. The breakout direction carries real gross (momentum) information beyond random sides and beyond the monthly long/short tilt, consistently in IS and VAL. The weakness is the net margin over costs.
issues.evidence: s02, 2000 seeds each, same engine, costs, risk (1.2x range width), time exit and no_overlap. N1 (coin-flip side at the candidate's signal times): IS PF median 0.906, max 1.146; 0/2000 pass IS or reach the candidate level; VAL pass 2.0%. N2 (random times with the candidate's time-of-day profile, random side): IS median 0.878, max 1.123; 0/2000; VAL pass 4.9%. Normal-tail estimate of P(IS pass) ≈ 1.1-1.3e-4 per trial, so P(≥1 of 370 at the candidate's IS level) ≈ 0.09 and with VAL ≈ 0.002. Candidate z vs N1: IS 3.49, VAL 1.94 (p 0.026). Side permuted within year / quarter / month: IS z 3.30 / 3.36 / 2.66, VAL z 1.72 / 1.76 / 1.81 (p 0.035 within month). Decomposition, R/trade: IS -0.067 random baseline + 0.047 monthly tilt + 0.141 within-month timing = 0.120; VAL -0.078 + 0.027 + 0.116 = 0.065.
issues.effect_on_results: Raises P(the gross signal is real) to about 0.85. It does not establish a net edge: timing ≈ +0.12-0.14 minus baseline cost ≈ 0.07-0.08 leaves a net that is a small difference of two noisy numbers.
