recommendations: Report the current-data numbers (IS PF 1.177, t 1.83, 6/9 years; VAL PF 1.1002, t 0.74), not the unpatched 1.196 / 1.115. State that the VAL pass is by 0.0002 PF and that resampling gives a 50% chance of passing.

Do not assign CONDITIONAL until the low-cost scenario is written down in COSTS.md / cost_scenarios.json first, as Amendment 1 requires, and evaluated consistently: scale the spread in the M1 frame before make_orders, or rebuild orders under the scenario quotes. audit.py and holdout.py apply spread_mult only inside simulate on pre-built orders; for this strategy that drops about 7% of fills and gives VAL PF 1.006 instead of 1.147.

Pre-register the holdout reading now. PF > 1 is weak (LR ≤ 2). Count it as support only if PF ≥ ~1.4, and as a meaningful negative only if PF ≤ ~0.8. Report gold's 2026 10-month move next to it, because in ≥15%-move windows even a zero-net version shows PF > 1 64% of the time. Also report the every-signal variant, the side split, and a 5-10% dropout distribution.

Treat the edge as unproven: a real but small gross momentum effect (about +0.12-0.14 R/trade of timing value) against roughly 0.07-0.08 R/trade of costs. Do not automate or size up on it. Alert-only paper trading should expect about PF 1.05 ± 0.25 per 10 months; if signals are missed, the expected PF drops to about 1.06-1.08 even under H1.
Do not rescue it with more filters. Every regime split (volatility, trendiness, trend alignment, MA60 x side) reverses between IS and VAL, and any new filter would be another fork in the search.

For project-level reporting: count VAL accesses and use M_eff-based family-wise p-values (ORB ≈ 23 effective of 48). Replace the audit's DSR (cross-trial SR variance) with the 1/T-variance version (0.32-0.44 here). Report random-effects-across-years t (1.12) alongside iid t. Weight neighbour robustness by independence: neighbours with corr < 0.8 have median PF 1.08.

reviews.lens: LIVE-EXECUTION REALISM (MT5 retail account, EU/ESMA, French client): manual delays, human availability, server clock/DST, rollover spreads, sizing/margin, MT5 implementation pitfalls, EA specification
reviews.verdict: Live-implementable only as an EA, or by a trader at the screen 08:00-13:00 Paris who acts within ~15 min. It also needs a low-cost ECN account, the exact one-position/first-touch policy, DST-correct London/NY clocks and a cancelled OCO leg. At primary-model costs, any one realistic friction drops VAL below 1.10 (current-data margin is only 0.0002). A salaried manual trader gets VAL PF 0.92-1.03 (primary costs) or 1.02-1.17 (low-cost broker).

issues.description: The edge exists only under the backtest's exact position policy: take the first touch of the day only if flat at that moment, no second chance, never overlap, never reverse. Natural EA or discretionary alternatives remove it, and an alert-first trader who 'decides' or keeps overlapping positions in a hedging account is running one of them.
issues.evidence: p8_ea_logic.out / p11_lowcost.out. V1 replica = baseline (verified identical): IS 1.177 / VAL 1.100. V2 'arm only if flat at 07:00 London': 1.170 / 1.108 (harmless). V3 every signal (hedging): 1.049 / 1.012 (low-cost ECN 1.180 / 1.119). V4 newest signal closes the old one: 0.958 / 0.877 (low-cost 1.097 / 0.978). V5 reverse on an opposite signal only: 1.072 / 0.953.
issues.effect_on_results: A policy deviation moves PF by -0.10 to -0.22. That is larger than any cost or timing friction tested. Live results are only comparable to the backtest if the EA enforces V1 or V2 exactly and logs every skipped or vetoed signal.

issues.description: Human availability. All 2,621 signals (first touches) fall on weekdays 08:00-13:00 Paris, 46% of them in 08:00-09:00. The requested windows (07-23 Paris any day, weekdays 08-20) therefore keep 100% of signals and leave PF unchanged. The real constraint is a salaried trader who cannot act 09:00-12:00 Paris.
issues.evidence: p2_availability.out, p11_lowcost.out, p12_account_types.out. Pre-work 08-09 Paris only: IS 1.085 (n 636) / VAL 0.924 (low-cost 1.216 with t 1.67 / 1.020). Pre-work + lunch 12-13: 1.035 / 0.955 (low-cost 1.171 / 1.051). 09-12 signals executed at market at 12:00 Paris: 1.116 / 0.999 (low-cost 1.248 / 1.134); with a next-morning exit added: 1.089 / 1.033 (low-cost 1.226 / 1.170). PF by Paris entry hour is unstable across periods: IS 08h 1.09, 09h 1.26, 10h 1.34, 11h 1.34, 12h 0.95; VAL 08h 1.07, 09h 0.77, 10h 1.28, 11h 1.76, 12h 2.24.
issues.effect_on_results: Manual execution by someone with a day job fails VAL at primary costs (PF 0.92-1.03) and is marginal even at the low-cost broker. The rule needs an EA or a trader at the screen all morning.

issues.description: At primary costs there is no buffer for live frictions. On the current (patched) data the baseline is IS PF 1.177 (t 1.83, 6/9 years), not the documented 1.196 / t 1.99 / 7/9. VAL PF is 1.10018, a pass by 0.0002. Every realistic friction tested pushes VAL below 1.10 on its own.
issues.evidence: p0_baseline.out, p1c_abs_artifact.out (unrounded PF), p6_pitfalls.out, p9_combos.out. Extra round-trip cost per oz: +$0.10 gives IS 1.153 / VAL 1.086; +$0.25 gives 1.119 / 1.066; +$0.50 gives 1.065 / 1.034. Retail swap 8% long / 2% short per year: 1.161 / 1.082; 10% / 4%: 1.138 / 1.060. Each $0.10/oz costs about 0.024 IS PF. IS reaches PF ≥ 1.20 with t ≥ 2 only if all-in costs are at least $0.10/oz below the model (IS 1.202, t 2.05). Account types, scenario-consistent and matching the recomputed official audit: low_cost_ecn 1.315 (t 2.96) / 1.210; typical_retail 1.226 (t 2.26) / 1.137; conservative 1.080 / 1.004.
issues.effect_on_results: The CONDITIONAL status holds on current data, but in practice the broker's real all-in cost decides viability. Phase 2 must verify spread, stop slippage and swap against the low_cost_ecn assumptions before trusting any live PF.

issues.description: Manual market entry N minutes after the stop would have filled. Within 15 minutes there is no systematic price decay (the delayed fill is only 0.006-0.015 R worse), but PF jitters by about ±0.03-0.06 depending on which trades flip or get skipped. That jitter is the size of the margin to both thresholds. Delays of 60 minutes or more degrade IS; 3-4 hours removes the edge.
issues.evidence: p1_delay.out, p1b_delay_sweep.out, p11_lowcost.out. Primary costs, same stop distance / same absolute stop, IS then VAL: N=1 1.184/1.163 and 1.080/1.101; N=5 1.218/1.177 and 1.010/1.098; N=15 1.214/1.164 and 1.050/1.089; N=60 1.078/1.122 and 1.135/1.090; N=240 0.995/0.997 and 1.051/1.073. Sweep N=1..15, same distance: IS 1.182-1.222, VAL 1.001-1.128, only 3 of 15 delays keep VAL ≥ 1.10. Same absolute stop: IS 1.152-1.182, VAL 1.088-1.109. Low-cost ECN, same distance: N=1/5/15/60/240 IS 1.336/1.370/1.364/1.197/1.114, VAL 1.208/1.140/1.197/1.222/1.141.
issues.effect_on_results: At the low-cost broker, a manual trader who acts within 15-60 min keeps the backtest's PF. At primary costs, a delay of only a few minutes is enough to decide pass or fail at VAL. An alert should be marked 'do not chase' after about 15 min.

issues.description: Clock and DST mapping. The range uses London time, the exit New York time, and the MT5 server is UTC+2/+3. The M1/H1 bar grid of a UTC+2/+3 server is identical to the UTC grid (whole-hour offsets), and this finalist uses no D/H4 bars, so 'server-grid bars' do not matter in themselves. What breaks results is an EA that hard-codes server or UTC hours. The US/EU DST gap covers 15-20 weekday sessions a year.
issues.evidence: p3_clock.out, p11_lowcost.out. NY-close server with fixed hours 02-09 / 14 / 23 (range becomes 23:00-06:00 London in gap weeks; 62 trades change): IS 1.142 / VAL 1.085 (low-cost 1.276 / 1.193). EET server with fixed hours: range exact, but in gap weeks the exit lands at 17:00 NY when the market is closed and fills at the 18:00 reopen: 1.177 / 1.098. Fixed UTC with no DST: 1.171 / 0.981 (low-cost 1.303 / 1.097). Range on winter hours all summer: 1.183 / 0.995 (low-cost 1.311 / 1.108).
issues.effect_on_results: A common EA shortcut costs up to 0.12 VAL PF. The only way to protect against this is to compute London and NY times from UTC with explicit EU and US DST rules. Note also that MT5's Strategy Tester returns TimeGMT() equal to simulated server time, so tester validation of DST handling is not sufficient.

issues.description: The broker's quotes are not Dukascopy's. The Asian range (max Ask / min Bid) and the first touch depend on quote details. Wider Asian-session retail spreads push both levels outward and hurt VAL. MT5 M1 bars are Bid-based, so the Ask high needs ticks.
issues.evidence: p7_feed.out, p11_lowcost.out. Broker Asian spread x2 while the range forms (levels about $0.20 wider): IS 1.181 / VAL 1.041. Levels +1 bp wider: 1.175 / 1.016; 1 bp narrower: 1.204 / 1.122. Random per-session feed noise σ 0.25 / 0.5 / 1 bp, 40 seeds each: VAL p5-p95 1.080-1.109 / 1.070-1.112 / 1.045-1.112, VAL ≥ 1.10 in 42 / 30 / 15% of seeds; IS ≥ 1.20 in 3 / 7 / 10%. Low-cost ECN with σ 0.5 bp: IS 1.295-1.331 / VAL 1.172-1.219 (100% pass). Range from Bid bars: 1.181 / 1.110. Bid high + 07:00 spread: 1.172 / 1.099.
issues.effect_on_results: At primary costs the VAL pass is a coin flip under realistic feed differences; at the low-cost broker it is robust. The EA's range definition must be fixed and the backtest re-run with that exact definition, ideally on the broker's own data.

issues.description: MT5 has no native OCO. With manual pending orders and no EA, or an EA that fails to delete the second leg, the opposite stop order sits at exactly the stop-loss price of the first trade. When the first trade is stopped before 12:00 London, a second position opens, in both hedging and netting accounts.
issues.evidence: p8_ea_logic.out: 122 of 1,483 sessions are stopped before 12:00 London. The second legs have IS PF 0.636 (n 92) / VAL 0.553 (n 30). Total with second legs: IS 1.123 / VAL 1.056.
issues.effect_on_results: About -0.05 PF. A salaried trader who places the OCO pair at 08:00 Paris by hand cannot cancel in time, so this is the realistic outcome for unassisted semi-manual execution.

issues.description: Practical sizing. Stops are 1.2x the Asian range and widened sharply in 2025, so the 0.01-lot (1 oz) minimum binds for small accounts. Drawdown depth and duration are also hard for a retail trader to sit through.
issues.evidence: p5_sizing.out. 2025 stop distance: median $32.20/oz (p10 $17.0, p90 $62.2, max $86.4; 0.96% of price), against $7.28 in IS. Account needed for 0.01 lot: $3,220 (median) / $6,216 (p90) / $8,638 (max) at 1% risk; $6,440 / $12,433 / $17,276 at 0.5%. With $5k, 25% (1%) or 61.5% (0.5%) of 2025 signals cannot be sized. With $10k at 0.5%, 25% cannot be sized and the realised median risk is 0.38%. Forcing the minimum lot on $1k means up to 8.6% risk. ESMA 1:20 margin is not binding (median 2-5% of equity, max 13.3%). Max drawdown: IS 51.5R (23.1% at 0.5%, 41.5% at 1%), VAL 40.2R (18.7% / 34.8%). Losing streaks 16 / 11. Longest time between equity highs: 1,310 days (IS) / 921 days (VAL).
issues.effect_on_results: An account of about $9-10k (1%) or $17-20k (0.5%) is needed to follow the rule as tested. Smaller accounts must skip signals they cannot size, which changes the path. The multi-year underwater periods make abandonment likely.

issues.description: Rollover spreads. Gold is closed 17:00-18:00 NY in the data. The x2 stress hits the 16:00 NY time exit (38% of trades) and stops near the break or reopen. The stops are wide, so stop hunting by spread spikes is negligible.
issues.effect_on_results: About -0.01 PF at x2. Only large sustained widening around the 16:00 NY exit matters.

issues.description: Pending-order expiry misuse. ORDER_TIME_DAY expires at server day end (17:00 NY), not 12:00 London, so the entry window silently stretches by about 10 hours. Some brokers do not allow ORDER_TIME_SPECIFIED on metals (SYMBOL_EXPIRATION_MODE).
issues.evidence: p13_expiry.out. Entry window to 13:00 London: IS 1.132 / VAL 1.091. To 16:00 London: 1.140 / 1.135. To 22:00 London (≈ ORDER_TIME_DAY): 1.153 / 1.075, with 314 extra afternoon fills (low-cost 1.257 / 1.176). Correctly expired windows still see 25 / 44 of 1,483 fills in the last 15 / 30 minutes before 12:00 London.
issues.effect_on_results: -0.02 to -0.05 PF, plus a different trade set.

issues.description: Closed-market exits and weekend gaps.
issues.evidence: p6_pitfalls.out, p10_misc.out, p8_ea_logic.out. 27 of 564 time exits fall in a closed market (US holidays, early closes, Good Friday) and fill at the 18:00 NY reopen or later. Positions crossed 315 weekend or holiday gaps; adverse gap p1 -0.77R, worst -1.39R, none jumped a stop (minimum room before a gap 0.08R; 4 cases under 0.25R). Only 2 of 919 stops filled beyond the stop by more than 0.01R (0.41R in total; worst trade -1.40R). Splitting by schedule, Thu/Fri entries give IS 1.092 / VAL 1.169 and Mon-Wed entries 1.240 / 1.050, so no consistent weekend effect. Note that a naive 'held over the weekend' split shows PF 5.9 vs 0.78 purely through survivorship.
issues.effect_on_results: Historically negligible, but the tail is real: a -1.4R Sunday gap with less room would have jumped a stop. The EA must handle TRADE_RETCODE_MARKET_CLOSED at the exit time and retry at the reopen.

issues.description: Not binding: StopsLevel/FreezeLevel, data completeness, fill-time spreads, trailing stop.
issues.evidence: p6_pitfalls.out, p10_misc.out. Distance from the market to the nearer pending level at 07:00 London: IS p1 $0.44 (1.9% under $0.50); 2025 p1 $1.38 (0% under $0.50). Stop-loss distance p1: $2.93 IS / $9.43 in 2025. A level is never already crossed at 07:00. Range minutes present: median 420 of 420; 11 of 3,354 sessions under 90%. Completeness guard 0.9 / 0.97 gives IS 1.177 / 1.174 with VAL unchanged. 69 fills in 07:00-07:04 London; spread at fill relative to the day's median has p90 1.15. The rule has no trailing stop.
issues.effect_on_results: None material. Do not add a terminal trailing stop: it runs client-side only and changes the rule.

issues.description: Method caveat: R-normalisation artifact for manual entry with the absolute stop after long delays. When price drifts back toward the fixed stop, remaining risk shrinks and R balloons.
issues.evidence: p1c_abs_artifact.out: VAL N=90 / 120 show R-based PF 1.398 / 1.483 with max R 61.1 / 43.6, against $-PF 1.29 / 1.24. Excluding trades with risk under 50% of the designed risk: 1.224 / 1.176.
issues.effect_on_results: Long-delay absolute-stop R-PFs overstate results and would imply huge positions at fixed % risk. Do not read them as an improvement, and do not adopt a 'skip if retraced' filter: it was not pre-registered.

recommendations: Do not run this rule manually if the trader has a day job. Phase 1 should be an EA in SHADOW mode: it computes everything, places nothing, sends alerts and journals. Manual execution is acceptable only if the trader is at the screen every weekday 08:00-13:00 Paris and enters within 15 min of the alert. After 15 min, skip the signal and do not chase.

Broker and account: use a low-cost raw/ECN MT5 account, the only setting in which the CONDITIONAL label holds. Before trusting any result, verify in the journal over the first 2-3 months: spread at 07:00-12:00 London of about $0.10-0.20, stop-entry slippage ≤ 0.75 bp, long swap ≤ about 4.6%/yr, and the reopen spread. A standard account (typical_retail) also passes on current data, with a thin margin (VAL 1.137).

Enforce the backtest policy exactly: at most one position; only the first touch of each level each day counts; if a position is open at the moment of the touch, the day is skipped with no re-entry or second chance; never overlap, reverse or replace. 'Arm at 07:00 London only if flat' is an acceptable variant (1.170 / 1.108). Every discretionary veto must be journalled with a reason.
OCO: delete the other leg in OnTradeTransaction as soon as one fills, then verify the deletion. Never leave a stop order resting at the stop-loss price, in either a netting or a hedging account.

Expiry: give pending orders ORDER_TIME_SPECIFIED expiry at 12:00 London converted to server time. Check SYMBOL_EXPIRATION_MODE first; if specified expiry is not allowed, the EA deletes the orders at 12:00 London and retries if FreezeLevel refuses. Never use ORDER_TIME_DAY or GTC.

Clocks: derive London and New York wall-clock times from UTC (TimeGMT() live) with explicit EU and US DST rules. Never hard-code server hours. Log the measured server offset (TimeTradeServer() - TimeGMT()) at every event. In the Strategy Tester, TimeGMT() equals simulated server time, so supply the broker's DST policy as an input there. Use M1 bars or ticks: server H4 bars (00/04/08) do not align with the 00:00-07:00 London range (02:00-09:00 server in normal weeks).

Range definition: Ask high and Bid low come from ticks (CopyTicksRange with COPY_TICKS_INFO, recomputed after any restart), not from MT5 bars, which are Bid-based. Persist H, L, the armed flag and the traded-today flag (file or GlobalVariables). Journal the range from both ticks and Bid bars. Before go-live, re-run the lab backtest with the EA's exact definition on the broker's own exported M1 and tick history.

Time exit: close at the first tradable tick at or after 16:00 New York on the 2nd weekday after the entry date (skip weekends, not holidays). On TRADE_RETCODE_MARKET_CLOSED, retry at the reopen. For manual fallback, pre-commit to either 20:00 Paris (1.165 / 1.105) or next-day 08:00 Paris (1.142 / 1.151); the time exit is not the fragile part.

ea_spec: Instrument and account: XAUUSD on an MT5 raw/ECN account (1 lot = 100 oz). One position at a time under the EA's magic number; hedging and netting accounts both work. The CONDITIONAL premise assumes: spread about 0.35x Dukascopy ($0.10-0.20), commission <= $7/lot round trip, stop/market slippage <= 0.75 bp per side, long swap <= 4.6%/yr, no short-swap credit.

Clocks: derive Europe/London and America/New_York wall-clock time from UTC (TimeGMT() live), with explicit DST rules: EU last Sunday of March to last Sunday of October at 01:00 UTC; US second Sunday of March to first Sunday of November at 02:00 local. Never hard-code server hours. In the Strategy Tester TimeGMT() returns server time, so supply the broker's GMT offset and DST rule as an input there. Log TimeTradeServer() - TimeGMT() at every event.

Range (each weekday, London date D): H = max Ask and L = min Bid over ticks in [00:00, 07:00) London, from CopyTicksRange. MT5 M1 bars are Bid-only, so the Ask high must come from ticks. W = H - L. No trade if W <= 0 or fewer than 210 of the 420 range minutes have quotes. Persist H, L and the day state, and recompute from ticks after any restart. A Bid-bar range is an acceptable fallback only if frozen before go-live (IS 1.181 / VAL 1.110).

Levels and stop: BuyLevel = H + 0.10*W (triggers on Ask); SellLevel = L - 0.10*W (triggers on Bid). A long's SL = SellLevel and a short's SL = BuyLevel, as absolute prices (risk about 1.2*W). No target, no break-even, no trailing stop. If a fill lands at or beyond its SL (a gap), close at market immediately.

Entry window [07:00, 12:00) London. If flat at 07:00, place a BuyStop at BuyLevel and a SellStop at SellLevel, each with its SL attached and ORDER_TIME_SPECIFIED expiry at 12:00 London converted to server time. If SYMBOL_EXPIRATION_MODE forbids specified expiry, the EA deletes the orders at 12:00 London and retries until confirmed. Never use ORDER_TIME_DAY or GTC. If a level is inside SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL of the price, trigger that leg virtually with a market order on the first tick at or through the level.
OCO: on the first fill, delete the other leg in OnTradeTransaction and verify the deletion. Never leave a pending order resting at the open position's SL price.

Position policy, exactly as backtested (V1): only the day's FIRST touch of either level counts. If a position is open at 07:00, place nothing but track touches virtually. If that position closes before any touch and before 12:00 London, place the OCO pair then. If the first touch comes while a position is open, or in the same minute it exits, the day is consumed: no second chance, never overlap, reverse or replace. The only acceptable simplification is 'arm only if flat at 07:00' (V2: IS 1.170 / VAL 1.108), and it must be chosen before go-live.

Time exit: close at the first tradable tick at or after 16:00 New York on the 2nd weekday after D (Mon->Wed, Thu->Mon, Fri->Tue). Weekends are skipped; holidays are not. On TRADE_RETCODE_MARKET_CLOSED (US holiday or early close), retry at the reopen. This matches the backtest; the longest IS hold was 159 h.

Sizing: lots = floor(risk% x equity / (|level - SL| x 100 oz x USD->account FX) / 0.01) x 0.01, computed on the planned distance. If that is below 0.01 lot, skip the signal and journal it; never force the minimum lot. Recommended risk is 0.5%: max drawdown 51.5R is about 23% at 0.5%, with losing streaks of 16 and up to 3.6 years underwater. With 2025-size stops (median $32/oz, max $86/oz) that needs about $17-20k of equity (about $9-10k at 1%).

Phase 3: automatic trading on demo. After 2-3 months, the measured 07:00-12:00 London spread, stop-entry slippage, commission and swap must be at or below the low_cost_ecn assumptions; if not, the CONDITIONAL premise has failed and trading stops.

Regime dependence: profit follows gold's trend years (correlation 0.78 between yearly long-minus-short R and gold's annual return), and range years (2018, 2021, 2022) lose. A 10-month holdout largely measures whether gold trended in 2026.
